It has not been cooked or tested by this project, has had no professional food-safety review and is not publication-ready. Times and temperatures are starting points. Air fryers differ; check the food and follow your appliance manual and any product cooking instructions.
summary: Vegetarian. Broccoli florets and other firm vegetables cooked at high heat until the edges brown. Under 15 minutes, using one mixing bowl.

ingredients.note: For frozen florets, follow the packet’s cooking instructions; adding 3 minutes is only a starting estimate and does not establish thorough cooking.

ingredients.item: Capsicum, red onion or zucchini, cut into 2 cm pieces
ingredients.note: Any firm vegetable of a similar size. Keep the pieces as big as the florets so everything finishes together.

ingredients.item: Grated hard cheese or a squeeze of lemon, to finish
ingredients.note: For a vegetarian kitchen, buy a hard cheese whose label says it is made without animal rennet, or use the lemon instead.

method.instruction: Toss the broccoli and the other vegetables with the oil and the seasoning in a bowl until every piece is lightly coated. Coat dry patches to reduce scorching.
Set the air fryer to 190°C, preheating only if your appliance manual requires it.
Tip the vegetables into the basket in as close to a single layer as you can manage. Crowding traps steam and limits browning; use two batches if needed.

Cook for 8 to 10 minutes, shaking at about 5 minutes. Tender thick stems and browned tips are texture cues, not a blanket safety test. Frozen vegetable packets may require thorough cooking: follow those instructions even if the outside has browned.

Finish with the cheese or lemon off the heat. After cooking, switch off, unplug and let the appliance cool before cleaning. Follow its manual for removable parts, soaking and cleaning products; never immerse the electrical unit or assume water alone is enough.

yield_note: A side for two, or a lunch bowl for one with rice or noodles. About 15 minutes in total. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.
provenance_note: Original practical notes written for this repository, with no outside source cited. Quantities suit a small household batch in a domestic air fryer and have not been checked in a test kitchen.

caveats: Vegetables are not automatically safe regardless of handling or cooking. Follow product storage and preparation instructions; frozen products may require thorough cooking, and browning alone does not establish that.

Light pieces may lift into the element in some models. Oil coating does not guarantee against fan lift. Follow the manual’s loading restrictions and do not use ingredients or loose liners that the appliance cannot safely retain.
The basket and drawer stay hot well after the machine stops. Set them down on a heatproof surface, not on a bench or a chopping board.
These are practical notes. Nothing here has been kitchen-tested by this project or given a professional food-safety review.
